players.comment: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday. Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports. Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

Wade (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game in Orlando. With both Wade and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) out for Wednesday's game, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope could draw a spot-start, and there will be more minutes available for Jabari Walker and Justin Edwards. Wade's next chance to play will come Saturday against the Bucks.

Brown (hamstring) will be re-evaluated at some point this weekend, per Kris Rihm of ESPN.com. It sounds like the 76ers are bracing for Brown, who is out for Wednesday's game against the Magic with a left hamstring strain, to be sidelined for multiple games. The star forward should be re-evaluated prior to Saturday's matchup versus the Bucks, and more usage should fall into the hands of Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and LeBron James for as long as Brown is on the shelf.

Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

Head coach JJ Redick said Reaves' (heel) pregame workout went "well," but he remains without an official timetable to return, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports. Given that Reaves' workout went "well" and the injury has been classified as a "heel bruise," we'd take the "no timetable" comment from Redick with a grain of salt. For now, Reaves should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Kings.

Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

players.comment: Maxey (foot) is out for Wednesday's game in Orlando, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports. Maxey will join Jaylen Brown (hamstring) on the inactive list for Wednesday's game, and it'll be Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope starting in their place. For now, Maxey should be considered questionable for Saturday's meeting with the Bucks.

Gardner (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game against the Bucks. Gardner was already in line to hit the bench in Pelle Larsson's (illness) return. He'll have some extra time to recover ahead of Sunday's showdown with the Thunder.

players.comment: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports. Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

players.comment: Lively (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. Lively remains out indefinitely due to 2025 foot surgery. Meanwhile, Daniel Gafford is locked in as Dallas' top center.

Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

Barlow (back) is out for Wednesday's game against Orlando. Barlow will be re-evaluated later this week and is thought to be closing in on his season debut, but he's not ready for game action quite yet. His next chance to return from a stress reaction in his back comes Saturday versus the Bucks.

Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

Raynaud (knee) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Suns. Raynaud continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff, suggesting he's still not close. He should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

players.comment: Bona (back) will be re-evaluated in approximately one week after seeing a specialist, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports. The fact that Bona needed to see a specialist suggests the injury may be more significant than initially thought, and he'll remain sidelined for at least the next several games. Even when healthy, the big man has seen his role shrink with Joel Embiid (foot) back in the rotation, averaging just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons in late October. In Bona's absence, Jabari Walker could see a few more minutes as Philadelphia's backup center.

Lawal is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors due to tightness in his right groin. It sounds like the rookie forward is dealing with a minor issue. His next chance to suit up comes Saturday against the Clippers.

Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.
